title: Is This Just Fantasy? Language Model Representations Reflect Human Judgments of Event Plausibility
abstract: arXiv:2507.12553v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Language models (LMs) are used for a diverse range of tasks, from question answering to writing fantastical stories. In order to reliably accomplish these tasks, LMs must be able to discern the modal category of a sentence (i.e., whether it describes something that is possible, impossible, completely nonsensical, etc.). However, recent studies have called into question the ability of LMs to categorize sentences according to modality (Michaelov et al., 2025; Kauf et al., 2023). In this work, we identify linear representations that discriminate between modal categories within a variety of LMs, or modal difference vectors. Analysis of modal difference vectors reveals that LMs have access to more reliable modal categorization judgments than previously reported. translated_title: 这仅仅是幻想吗？语言模型表征反映人类对事件合理性的判断
translated_abstract: 语言模型被用于各种多样的任务，从问答到撰写奇幻故事。为了可靠地完成这些任务，语言模型必须能够辨别句子的情态范畴（即，句子描述的是可能发生的事、不可能发生的事，还是完全荒谬的内容等）。然而，近期的研究对语言模型依据情态对句子进行分类的能力提出了质疑（Michaelov et al., 2025; Kauf et al., 2023）。在这项工作中，我们在多种语言模型中识别出了能够区分不同情态范畴的线性表征，即情态差异向量。对情态差异向量的分析表明，语言模型所具备的情态分类判断能力比之前报道的更为可靠。此外，我们发现情态差异向量随着模型能力的提升（即通过训练步数、层数和参数量的增加）以一致的顺序涌现。值得注意的是……
tldr: 本研究识别出语言模型中用于区分句子情态范畴（可能、不可能、荒谬等）的线性表征——情态差异向量，证明语言模型的情态判断能力比以往认知更可靠，且这些向量随模型能力增强以一致的顺序涌现。
en_tdlr: This work identifies linear representations called modal difference vectors that discriminate between modal categories in language models, revealing that LMs possess more reliable modal categorization judgments than previously reported, and that these vectors emerge in a consistent order as models become more competent.
